text: 69-year-old male. The patient presents with pain in his left great toe, hips, and knees that worsens with activity and improves with rest. He reports that the symptoms have progressively gotten worse over the past several years.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of gout or high uric acid levels, or do the joints appear red, hot, and swollen during flare-ups? I also need to know if you have any morning stiffness that lasts longer than 30 minutes.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your age and the pattern of pain worsening with activity, I suspect osteoarthritis rather than gout or inflammatory arthritis. To confirm this and rule out other causes, I need to see the structural state of your joints. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of the left great toe, hips, and knees.
